title: What a backfill does with an unsafe verdict, and how its window is measured

options.name: Keep current behaviour: backfilled unsafe verdicts schedule live exits (contrary to the D-BACKFILL comments); the window starts at the last subscription
options.risk: Most reconnects after a long session skip the outage replay (GAP DETECTED); every registration replays already-handled logs (AUD-ANTIRUG-005).

options.name: Match the documented rule: backfill never exits, it alerts per still-held position with the stale evidence
options.behavior_impact: A rug missed during an outage produces an alert, not a sell.
options.risk: The operator has to sell by hand while the pool drains further.

options.name: Keep exiting on backfilled verdicts for still-held positions, but only after a fresh live re-read, and measure the window from the last live block
options.behavior_impact: Outage windows are replayed fully; still-held rugged positions get an exit attempt.
options.risk: An exit on old evidence can sell a pool that recovered (rare after a real LP pull).

recommendation: exit-if-held, with last_seen_block advanced from the live stream, after a Phase 23 test that drops the socket during a rug.
default: Keep current behaviour until the owning phase decides (milestone contract). This card covers S1 capital findings, which cannot rest on the default: until it is decided and fixed it blocks the live re-entry gate.
behavior_impact: Decides whether a rug that happened during a WebSocket outage is sold, alerted, or missed.
needed_by: Phase 24 discussion (capital fixes, after the Phase 23 real-path proof)
